newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Two Italian oilseed biofuel schemes illegal - EU.
newsitem.headline: Two Italian oilseed biofuel schemes illegal - EU.

text.p: The European Commission on Thursday said that two Italian schemes to promote the production of biofuel from oilseeds infringed EU rules.
The first scheme provided 150,000 lire per hectare for rapeseed and sunflower seed grown on set-aside land.
Under the second scheme, up to 125,000 tonnes annually of biofuel produced from oilseeds grown on set-aside land was exempted from excise duties.
"We are not against the production of biofuel but aid must be given according to the rules," a Commission spokesman said.
The Commission said in a statement that the two schemes infringed EU rules on a common market in fats and EU regulation 1765/92 on set-aside.
Although the first scheme was never applied, the second scheme has been in operation since January 1994.
The Italian government, which has already said it will amend its excise duty exemption scheme, was given two months to do so.
The new scheme must be approved by the European Commission.
